literal: To those who have acquired excellent wealth abundantly, the other two are easy things together.
translation: To those who have abundantly acquired glorious wealth, the other two values of life (virtue and pleasure) become easily attainable together.
modern: சிறந்த செல்வத்தை மிகுதியாக ஈட்டியவர்களுக்கு, மற்ற இரு உறுதிகளாகிய அறமும் இன்பமும் எளிதாகக் கிடைக்கக்கூடிய பொருள்களாக ஒருசேர அமைந்துவிடும்.
explanation: This couplet highlights the supreme practical utility of wealth in achieving the other goals of life. 'ஒண்பொருள்' refers to glorious, rightfully earned wealth, and 'காழ்ப்ப' means to accumulate it in solid abundance. For those who possess such wealth, the other two aspects of human life—virtue (அறம்) and pleasure (இன்பம்)—become 'எண்பொருள்' (easy things) that can be attained together ('ஒருங்கு') without arduous effort. Wealth serves as the enabling instrument that naturally brings righteous deeds and worldly happiness within one's reach.
